title: Filtered sheaf-colimit transfer of the canonical cyclic comparison
statement:
Let $R$ be a commutative condensed ring on the small coherent profinite site [sk-def-sfb-condensed-ring, def-weil-size-convention]. Let $H$ be a profinite group and $u:\mathbf Z_{\mathrm{disc}}\to H$ a continuous homomorphism; put $\tau=u(1)$. Use ordinary internal $R$-modules [sk-def-sfb-module-objects], the category $\mathcal A_H(R)$ of condensed $H$-actions [def-sfb-condensed-action-module], and ordinary right derived invariants in that full action category [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. For an action module $N$, let $K(N)=[N\xrightarrow{\tau-1}N]$ in degrees $0,1$ and let
$$c_N=(\lambda_N^1)^{-1}\beta_N^1:R\Gamma_H(N[0])\longrightarrow QK(N)$$
be the canonical cyclic restriction comparison of [lem-sfb-relative-cyclic-restriction-model], with trivial residual group.

Let $I$ be a small nonempty filtered category in the chosen compatible universes, let $(N_i)_{i\in I}$ be any diagram in $\mathcal A_H(R)$, and let $N=\operatorname{colim}_i N_i$ be its sheaf colimit with induced action. For every integer $q$, the maps induced by its actual coprojections give isomorphisms of internal $R$-modules
$$a_q:\operatorname{colim}_iH^q(R\Gamma_H(N_i[0]))\xrightarrow{\sim}H^q(R\Gamma_H(N[0])),\qquad
b_q:\operatorname{colim}_iH^q(QK(N_i))\xrightarrow{\sim}H^q(QK(N)).$$
They satisfy the equality
$$H^q(c_N)\circ a_q=b_q\circ\operatorname{colim}_iH^q(c_{N_i}).$$
In negative degrees both sides of each comparison are zero. In particular, if every $c_{N_i}$ is an isomorphism, then $c_N$ is an isomorphism. No injectivity of transition maps, finite generation, nilpotence, norm completeness, density of $u(\mathbf Z)$ or uniform cohomological-dimension bound is assumed; the colimit is not a completion or a colimit of topological section spaces.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-profinite-invariants-filtered-continuity] with $J=H$. The group is profinite, the diagram is small filtered in the compatible universes, and the coefficients are ordinary internal modules, exactly as required there. Its creation clause identifies its action colimit with the stated sheaf colimit $N$. For every $q\geq0$ its canonical isomorphism is $a_q$, since its legs are precisely $H^q(R\Gamma_H(\iota_i[0]))$ for the actual coprojections $\iota_i:N_i\to N$.

proof.text: Write $d_i=\tau-1$ and $d=\tau-1$ on the underlying modules. Equivariance gives $d\iota_i=\iota_i d_i$, so the termwise colimit of the arrows $d_i$ is the arrow $d:N\to N$. Filtered colimits of these ring-sheaf modules are exact by [lem-pc-module-filtered-colimits-tensor]. Thus [lem-sfb-arrow-exact-colimits] identifies the colimits of their kernels and cokernels with $\ker d$ and $\operatorname{coker}d$, with the actual induced legs. Since $H^0(K(M))=\ker(\tau-1)$, $H^1(K(M))=\operatorname{coker}(\tau-1)$, and every other cohomology is zero, these are exactly the required $b_0,b_1$; for other $q$, $b_q$ is the unique isomorphism between zero objects. Cohomology after $Q$ is cohomology of complexes by [def-weil-abstract-derived-category].

proof.text: For $q<0$, [lem-sfb-condensed-derived-invariant-bar] represents $R\Gamma_H(M[0])$ by a total with compatible nonnegative resolutions in nonnegative bar degrees. Every total degree is therefore nonnegative, so its negative cohomology is zero, for $M=N$ and for every $M=N_i$. Colimits of zero diagrams are zero by the universal property. Together with step 2 this proves both negative-degree assertions, and defines $a_q$ there as the unique zero-object isomorphism.

proof.text: By [lem-sfb-relative-cyclic-restriction-model] with residual group $G=1$, $\beta$ is natural and $\lambda$ is a natural isomorphism. Inverting its naturality equation and composing with that of $\beta$ gives, for every $\iota_i$, the derived equality $c_N R\Gamma_H(\iota_i[0])=QK(\iota_i)c_{N_i}$. Let $j_i^A,j_i^B$ be the coprojections into the source and target cohomology colimits, and $C_q=\operatorname{colim}_iH^q(c_{N_i})$; naturality makes the latter a map of diagrams, so $C_qj_i^A=j_i^BH^q(c_{N_i})$. Applying $H^q$ to the derived equality and the leg equations from steps 1-3 yields $H^q(c_N)a_qj_i^A=b_qC_qj_i^A$. Uniqueness in the colimit universal property gives $H^q(c_N)a_q=b_qC_q$, including negative $q$.

proof.text: If every $c_{N_i}$ is invertible, their cohomology maps are invertible. Their inverses form a natural transformation (multiply the naturality equations by the inverses), and applying the colimit functor to the two inverse equations shows that $C_q$ is invertible. The square just proved gives $H^q(c_N)=b_qC_qa_q^{-1}$, hence every $H^q(c_N)$ is invertible. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-unbounded-derived-iso-cohomology] in the abelian category of internal $R$-modules to conclude that $c_N$ is invertible. No step used monic transitions, density, or a bound on cohomological dimension.
